entities.summary:
John I, Duke of Cleves, Count of Mark, Jean de Belliqueux (warlike), was a significant figure in the medieval European political landscape. Born in unknown year, he became Duke of Cleves and Count of Mark in 1368, succeeding his father, John II. His reign was marked by conflicts with neighboring territories, including the Duchy of Burgundy and the Electorate of Cologne.

John I's strategic alliances and military campaigns expanded the Duchy of Cleves' influence, but ultimately led to his downfall. The Duke was forced to abdicate in 1397, and his territories were divided among his sons, leading to a period of instability in the region.

Despite his limited territorial gains, John I's legacy as a military leader and politician has endured. His descendants continued to play a significant role in European politics, and his name remains associated with the Duchy of Cleves to this day.

The 14th-century chronicler, Arnold of Villenfels, wrote: "John I, Duke of Cleves, fought against the Burgundians, but ultimately was forced to surrender.", a testament to the enduring impact of his actions on the medieval world.
